shots.text: Disney bought a secret swamp using fake names.
You see, Walt Disney wanted to build a huge new park in Florida.
But if sellers heard the name Disney, every acre would cost a fortune.
So his team bought land through companies with names like Reedy Creek Ranch Corporation.
One company was even called M. T. Lott. Say it fast.
Swamp, scrub and cattle pasture went for less than two hundred dollars an acre.
Starting in nineteen sixty-four, parcel by parcel, they gathered more than twenty-seven thousand acres.
You see, that's about twice the size of Manhattan.
Then a reporter, Emily Bavar, asked Walt about the mystery buyer on a press trip in California.
In October nineteen sixty-five, her newspaper put it on the front page: the mystery buyer is Disney.
So weeks later, Walt, his brother Roy and Florida's governor announced it in Orlando.
Walt died in nineteen sixty-six. He never saw that swamp become Walt Disney World.
